chapter: Family lore, Boston and Europe with Sam Price
title: Grandmother's stories of slavery
summary: His sister Anna Mae recalls their grandmother, born in slavery, whose lips were stitched for talking back.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Tell me, did you ever recall your parents talking to you about your grandparents, or anything about your grandparents?

blocks.s: ANNA MAE ORANGE, SISTER OF JCH:

blocks.x: I knew of my grandparents. I knew my grandmother and I knew my grandfather.
Did they ever talk of slavery play with you?
My grandmother did. She talked and played of slavery.
What kind of things did she -

She said her father must have been white because I think - she was born in slavery, I know that. She was so white they wouldn't let her work on the farm. They had her to work in the big house, she said, and they couldn't control her temper. She used to sew and they would tell her to do different things and she wouldn't do it and she would talk back to them.
I remember one time she told me they stitched up her lips.
Really? And you told us the same story?
She wouldn't give in to them
I thought it was my aunt.
In that picture down the hall they could pass for twins. The last time I saw it, beautiful!
